newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIA DESPATCHES TWO PLANES TO CAMBODIA
The Prime Minister says the government has despatched two transport planes as part of a plan to evacuate Australians from Cambodia if necessary.
Mr Howard told Channel Nine one plane is now in Butterworth in Malaysia, and another will leave later today.
He says are about 517 Australians registered with the embassy in Phnom Penh, and the embassy has been in touch with them.
Mr Howard said none of them had been injured according to a report he received this morning and the government was making a lot of contingency arrangements.
Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Alexander Downer says he fears the international community can do little to end the fighting in Cambodia.
Mr Downer says Cambodia's Coalition Government has collapsed irretrievably, and it's unlikely the two warring leaders will be able to work together again.
An Australian envoy who left for Cambodia yesterday is now stranded in Vietnam, and it's doubtful he'll be able to enter the country.
Mr Downer says Australia can only repeat calls for Cambodia's leaders to stop fighting.
USING SUPERANNUATION FOR A HOME DEPOSIT
The Prime Minister says there are arguments in favour of allowing low-income earners to use their superannuation for a home deposit.
The Real Estate Institute and the Housing Industry Association say compulsory super payments are denying many Australians the chance to own their own home.
They've called on the Federal Government to relax superannuation laws to help people on incomes of about $30,000 a year.
Mr Howard says there are arguments in favour of the proposal and the government is examining the issue.
But he says if the government did agree to invest more funds in one sector, it might be more appropriate to target manufacturing, not housing, because of the impact on jobs.
PROVE INTO HOW TERRORIST WAS ALLOWED INTO AUSTRALIA
The Prime Minister says the Immigration Department is urgently investigating how a convicted American terrorist was allowed to enter Australia.
Former Black Panther activist, and convicted hijacker, Lorenzo Ervin, is in Brisbane after obtaining a visa to enter Australia.
He was convicted in 1969 of hijacking a plane to Cuba, and sentenced to two life-sentences, but later released.
Mr Howard says he was horrified when he heard Ervin was allowed into Australia, and told Radio 2GB he has taken steps to deal with the matter.
"I think it's quite wrong that somebody like that should have got into country in the first place, and it's the result of a misrepresentation," Mr Howard said.
But a lawyer seeking permission for Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams to enter Australia, says he believes Ervin is entitled to his visa.
Gerry Adams was denied a visa because of the Immigration Minister's concerns he was linked to the provisional IRA.
Mr Adam's lawyer, Terry Fisher, says he believes Mr Ervin is entitled to be in Australia on a Freedom of Speech basis, but the situation highlights the government's hypocrisy.

"The Government also allows in lots of Indonesian generals with proven track records in murdering people in East Timor, so I think the government is very selective in who it lets in and who it doesn't," Mr Fisher said.
PROSSER CLAIMS SUPPORT FROM SMALL BUSINESS AND COLLEAGUES
Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser says he has had overwhelming support from both the small business sector and government colleagues.
Mr Prosser is continuing to resist pressure from the Opposition for him to resign over allegations his private business interests conflict with his ministerial duties.
He says the whole affair is a beat up by Labor to cover its own leadership problems.
Mr Prosser told ABC Radio, business people want him to stay in the job.
He says the overwhelming number of small business people who have called him, have supported him.

Mr Prosser says small business people have been telling him they want a minister who understands small business and they are sick of having ministers who are either union people or professional politicians.
NO LIFE ON MARS SURFACE DECLARES AUSSIE PHYSICIST
Australian Physicist Paul Davies says the space vehicle on Mars will certainly not find any life forms in the area that it's investigating.
He says the surface of Mars is so barren that it's almost inconceivable anything would be living there now.
But, he says if there's any form of life on Mars, it's likely to be two or three kilometres underground.
He's told ABC Radio that underground would be a more suitable environment.
The physicist says it would take people drilling deep undergound with heavy equipment to find any organisms on Mars, and any such expedition will be a long time in the future.
SHANE WARNE COMING HOME TO SEE FAMILY
After becoming the most successful leg spinner in Test cricket, Shane Warne is to make a flying visit home to see his wife and new baby daughter.
Warne will make a one-week dash to Melbourne - to be back in time for Australia's next first-class match against Glamorgan at Cardiff starting on July 16.

Warne's innings of 6-48 in the third Test at the weekend took him past former Australian captain Richie Benaud's tally of 248 Test wickets, and made him the most successful leg-spinner in test history.
The bowler said he was pretty keen to see wife Simone, and new baby Brooke Victoria, as they had been on his mind.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
